name: Spare Food
replaces: Uber Eats, DoorDash and local apps such as Delivereasy
summary: Food delivery where restaurants pay only the at-cost fee, couriers keep their whole delivery fee and tips, and customers pay menu prices. Restaurants and couriers keep all the profit except running costs, and vote on its fees and rules.

areas.name: Accounts, sign-up and onboarding
areas.summary: One Spareware login for customers, restaurants and couriers, with only the checks each role needs before its first order or delivery.

features.name: Customer sign-up and sign-in
features.does: Create an account in under a minute with a passkey, email or phone, or order with just a phone number.

parts.name: Customer account profile
parts.what: Food's own fields on the kit profile: saved addresses, dietary preferences and access needs, the last two saved only with consent under Food's rules for sensitive details.

parts.name: Food sign-in set-up
parts.what: Uses the kit's passkey and code sign-in screens, asking only what an order needs: a name and a phone number.

parts.name: Quick account at checkout
parts.what: A light account made from a phone number at checkout, with an offer to finish it later; on a new device it shows no past orders, addresses or saved cards until the recycled number checks pass, and true guest orders wait for the guest order decision.

parts.name: Phone number required
parts.what: Food asks for a confirmed phone number before the first delivery order, using the kit's phone check.

parts.name: Recycled and spoofed number checks
parts.what: An account tied only to a phone number shows no order history, addresses or saved cards on a new device until a second check passes, such as a passkey or an email code; a number unused for a long time must be confirmed again, and texted codes go through the kit's text cost guard.

parts.name: Guest order decision
parts.what: Whether Food takes true guest orders with no account, weighing card fraud, anti-money-laundering duties and data rights; owned here until the kit opens one shared decision for every app.

features.name: Restaurant sign-up
features.does: A restaurant owner can apply, prove the business is real and registered for food safety, and go live.

parts.name: Restaurant application flow
parts.what: Steps for business details, address, trading hours, bank account and contact people.

parts.name: Business and owner checks
parts.what: Food's rule that a restaurant passes the kit's business number lookup, and its owner the kit's identity check, before going live.

parts.name: Food safety registration check
parts.what: Records the restaurant's food safety registration and its expiry (example: under New Zealand's Food Act), with reminders from the kit's re-check scheduler before it lapses.

parts.name: Restaurant payout set-up
parts.what: Sends the restaurant to the kit's payout set-up with the payment provider as part of the application.

parts.name: Restaurant approval
parts.what: Reviewers approve, query or decline each application, and every decision is an operation in the log.

features.name: Courier sign-up
features.does: A person can apply to deliver, pass the checks the law and the members set, and start the same week.

parts.name: Courier application flow
parts.what: Steps for identity, visa conditions, vehicle type, licence where needed, and payout account.

parts.name: Identity check
parts.what: Food's use of the kit's identity check, with the selfie match run under the biometric code (FOOD-A1-F3-P8) and the right-to-work result passed to the visa check.

parts.name: Driver licence and vehicle rules
parts.what: Food's rules for the licence class, registration and warrant or certificate of fitness each vehicle type needs, checked by the kit.

parts.name: Criminal record check
parts.what: Asks for a criminal record check, with the courier's consent, only where the kit's necessity test shows the law or the job's risk supports one; a member vote alone never makes it lawful.

parts.name: Courier terms step
parts.what: Shows the courier terms during sign-up and records which version was accepted.

parts.name: Getting-started lessons
parts.what: Food's short lessons on keeping food safe in transit, alcohol rules, road safety and using the app, with a short check at the end, on the kit's training and certificates.

parts.name: Visa conditions check
parts.what: Food's rules on the kit's visa entitlement check: whether a visa allows this kind of courier work under the status decision, any weekly hour limit such as a student visa's, and a re-check before it ends.

parts.name: Food's biometric code case
parts.what: Food's use of the kit's biometric code compliance: why selfie matching couriers is proportionate, Food's notice text, and a person reviewing every failed match.

parts.name: Non-biometric check option
parts.what: Food offers the kit's non-biometric route, a video or in-person check by a person, at sign-up and at every re-check.

features.name: One account, many roles
features.does: A person can be a customer, a courier and restaurant staff on one login, and switch between them.

parts.name: Restaurant roles
parts.what: Food's roles inside a restaurant (owner, manager, staff) on the kit's organisation model and roles per app.

parts.name: Staff invites
parts.what: Food's staff permission sets, such as taking orders without seeing payouts, on the kit's team management.

parts.name: Courier checks reused across apps
parts.what: Checks a person already passed in the kit, such as identity and licence, count for Food courier work where the law allows.

features.name: Free membership on joining
features.does: A restaurant or courier can become a voting member as part of signing up, free.

parts.name: Membership offer at sign-up
parts.what: Offers free membership during restaurant and courier sign-up, using the kit's join flow.

parts.name: Food member groups
parts.what: Which voting group restaurants and couriers join in the co-op-wide member list; the list itself is the kit's.

features.name: Account recovery and closing
features.does: A person can recover a lost login, or close an account with its data exported or erased.

parts.name: Recovery rules for payout holders
parts.what: Food asks for the kit's extra recovery checks for anyone who receives payouts, and holds payouts for a waiting period after a recovery.

parts.name: Close account
parts.what: Settles any Food balance and open orders first, then hands over to the kit's account deletion.

features.name: Minimum ages for each role
features.does: Each role has a published minimum age: couriers by vehicle type, and customer account holders.

parts.name: Minimum ages
parts.what: The minimum age for couriers on each vehicle type and for customer account holders, set on the kit's minimum age at sign-up.

parts.name: Age at sign-up
parts.what: Uses the date-of-birth result from the identity check to apply each role's minimum age.

features.name: Teen ordering paid by a parent
features.does: A teenager orders food with a parent paying, and is never shown restricted items.

parts.name: Teen accounts
parts.what: A parent links and pays for a teen account through the kit's delegated access, with alcohol and other restricted items hidden and blocked.

features.name: Home kitchens and food trucks
features.does: A home-based food business, or a food truck whose location changes, can sell through the app.

parts.name: Moving pickup location
parts.what: A vendor sets today's location and hours, and the delivery area check follows it.

parts.name: Home and mobile food business rules
parts.what: How home-based and mobile food businesses register under each country's food safety law (example: New Zealand's Food Act), and what their page must show.

areas.name: Finding food
areas.summary: How a customer finds what to eat: nearby restaurants, search, filters and a map, ranked by published rules with no paid placement.

features.name: Browse nearby restaurants
features.does: See which restaurants deliver to my address now, with the time, fee and rating for each.

parts.name: Delivery area check
parts.what: Work out which restaurants can deliver to an address from each restaurant's area and courier supply.

parts.name: Restaurant list and cards
parts.what: The home list showing name, photo, cuisine, time estimate, the full delivery cost and rating.

parts.name: Food ranking factors
parts.what: Food's factors (distance, time and rating) on the kit's published ranking rules, with no paid placement.

parts.name: Open and closed state
parts.what: Show opening hours, holiday closures and paused restaurants, with ordering ahead for later.

features.name: Search
features.does: Search for a restaurant, dish or cuisine and get sensible results even with spelling mistakes.

parts.name: Food search fields
parts.what: Restaurants, dishes and tags indexed in the kit's search service and updated as menus change.

parts.name: Search screen
parts.what: Search box with suggestions, recent searches, and results grouped by restaurant and dish.

parts.name: Macron-aware Food search
parts.what: Food's search uses the kit's accent-aware matching for names in each country's languages as restaurants write them (example: te reo Māori names with macrons in New Zealand), and indexes translated dish names once menus carry them.

features.name: Filters and dietary needs
features.does: Filter by cuisine, price, distance, rating, pickup, and dietary needs such as vegan, halal or gluten-free.

parts.name: Dietary and cuisine tags
parts.what: One shared list of tags restaurants apply to dishes and venues.

parts.name: Allergen filter
parts.what: Hides dishes that contain or may contain chosen allergens, using the restaurant's own declarations, never promises a dish is safe, and points to the allergy request.

parts.name: Filter and sort controls
parts.what: Filter chips and sort options on the list and search screens.

features.name: Map view
features.does: See restaurants on a map and choose by where they are.

parts.name: Restaurant map
parts.what: Restaurant pins on the kit's map display, on open map data.

features.name: Favourites and reorder
features.does: Save favourite restaurants and dishes, and reorder a past order in two taps.

parts.name: Favourite dishes
parts.what: Favourite dishes and restaurants for each customer, on the kit's favourites.

parts.name: Reorder from history
parts.what: Rebuild a past cart, flagging items that changed price or are no longer sold.

features.name: Restaurant page
features.does: See a restaurant's menu, hours, address, access details, rating, fees and food safety grade before ordering.

parts.name: Restaurant page layout
parts.what: Header, details, menu sections and reviews on one page.

parts.name: Food safety grade display
parts.what: Show the council's food grade where the council publishes one.

parts.name: Access details
parts.what: Step-free entry, where to collect and accessible parking for pickup, shown on the restaurant page.

parts.name: Trader details
parts.what: The restaurant's trading name, legal name and business number on its page and on every receipt, from the kit's trader details, so a customer knows who sold them the meal.

features.name: Collections and local picks
features.does: Browse lists such as new places, local favourites and late-night food, chosen by published rules or by members.

parts.name: Collections service
parts.what: Rule-based and member-chosen lists, with the rules published.

features.name: Suggestions a person controls
features.does: Get suggestions from my own past orders, and turn personalisation off with one switch.

parts.name: Food suggestion rules
parts.what: Suggestions from the customer's own past orders, on the kit's explainable suggestions, never sold, and never using allergies, faith-based diets or access needs unless the person switches that on.

parts.name: Personalisation switch
parts.what: One setting to turn personalised ranking off, and a note on why each suggestion appears.

areas.name: Menus and catalogue
areas.summary: Restaurants build and keep their menus up to date, with options, allergens, photos and stock, at the same prices as in store.

features.name: Build a menu
features.does: A restaurant can create sections and dishes with prices, descriptions and photos.

parts.name: Menu data model
parts.what: Sections, items, prices, tax, photos and availability as Food's own fields on the kit's listing model.

parts.name: Menu editor
parts.what: Food's menu editing (sections, dishes and drag to reorder) on the kit's listing editor, for browser and tablet.

parts.name: Dish photo rules
parts.what: Food's photo sizes and crops on the kit's file uploads.

parts.name: Menu import from files
parts.what: Imports a menu from the restaurant's own spreadsheet or point-of-sale export, in the open menu format where it can, for the restaurant to check, never from another platform's listing.

parts.name: Menu and photo rights
parts.what: Menus and photos come only from the restaurant's own files, never copied from other platforms' listings or photos, and each photo records who holds its rights.

parts.name: Open menu and order formats
parts.what: Compares open standards for menus and orders and ports the best fit instead of inventing one: Open Delivery from Brazil (its first repository is Apache-2.0; the licence of version 2 is *unverified*), the Beckn food and beverage specification (licence *unverified*) and schema.org's Menu types.

features.name: Options and add-ons
features.does: A restaurant can offer sizes, extras, choices and combos, with rules such as "pick two".

parts.name: Option groups
parts.what: Option groups with minimum and maximum choices, prices and nesting.

parts.name: Combos and meal deals
parts.what: Bundles of items at a set price.

features.name: Allergens and dietary information
features.does: A restaurant can declare allergens and dietary tags for every dish, and a customer can read them before ordering.

parts.name: Allergen fields
parts.what: The allergens the Food Standards Code lists, with plain-English names, on every dish, stored against an allergen list for each country.

parts.name: Allergen display and reminder
parts.what: Show allergens on each dish and remind the customer to tell the restaurant about an allergy.

parts.name: Online allergen duty
parts.what: What the Food Standards Code requires for food sold online, and who must provide it.

parts.name: Energy and nutrition details
parts.what: Optional kilojoules and nutrition details per dish.

parts.name: Cross-contact fields
parts.what: 'May contain' warnings on each dish, and shared fryers or surfaces for each kitchen.

features.name: Stock and availability
features.does: A restaurant can mark a dish sold out, sell dishes only at set times, and run separate breakfast or lunch menus.

parts.name: Sold-out switch
parts.what: One tap marks an item or option sold out until a chosen time.

parts.name: Time-based menus
parts.what: Menus and items available only on set days and times.

features.name: Same price as in store
features.does: A customer sees the restaurant's in-store prices, and the restaurant confirms it.

parts.name: Price match promise
parts.what: A restaurant states its prices match in store, shown as a badge, with a way for customers to report a difference.

features.name: Menus in many languages
features.does: A restaurant can add translations, or check machine translations before they go live.

parts.name: Translation fields
parts.what: Translated names and descriptions for each language.

parts.name: Suggested translations
parts.what: Machine translation from the kit's translation service at cost, labelled as machine-made and offered for the restaurant to check before publishing.

features.name: Many locations and brands
features.does: A restaurant group can share one menu across locations with local prices, stock and hours.

parts.name: Shared menu with local changes
parts.what: One main menu with price, stock and hours set per location.

features.name: Menu sync with point of sale
features.does: A restaurant using a point-of-sale system keeps its menu and stock in step automatically.

parts.name: Point-of-sale menu sync
parts.what: Pull menus and stock from point-of-sale systems that have open, licensable interfaces.

features.name: Menu checks
features.does: Menus are checked for missing allergen details, restricted items, hidden instructions to AI agents and obvious mistakes before going live.

parts.name: Automatic menu checks
parts.what: Flags missing allergens, zero prices and duplicate dishes, and blocks alcohol and other age-restricted items until alcohol delivery (FOOD-A14-F2) is built.

parts.name: Hidden instruction checks
parts.what: Flags menu text, dish names and reviews that address AI agents, such as telling assistants to always choose this restaurant, and marks all menu text as data for the kit's hidden instruction guards.

features.name: Brands show their real kitchen
features.does: A customer sees which real kitchen cooks for every brand, including delivery-only brands.

parts.name: Kitchen behind each brand
parts.what: Every brand links to the registered kitchen that cooks it, shown on its page with that kitchen's food safety grade.

features.name: Packaging charges and rules
features.does: A restaurant charges for bags or containers on their own line, and menus follow local single-use plastic rules (example: New Zealand's phase-outs).

parts.name: Packaging charge line
parts.what: A bag or container charge shown as its own line before checkout.

parts.name: Single-use plastic rules
parts.what: Which takeaway packaging each country's single-use plastic rules cover, turned into menu checks, starting with New Zealand's phase-outs.

features.name: Menu from a photo or PDF
features.does: A restaurant photographs its paper menu or uploads a PDF, and checks the dishes it reads before they go live.

parts.name: Menu reading
parts.what: Reads dishes, prices and options from a menu photo or PDF with the co-op's AI at cost, and publishes nothing until the restaurant checks it.

areas.name: Ordering and checkout
areas.summary: Everything between choosing a dish and paying: the cart, delivery or pickup, address, time, notes and a clear price breakdown.

features.name: Cart
features.does: Add dishes with their options, change amounts and see the running total.

parts.name: Cart model
parts.what: Items, options, notes and totals for one restaurant, kept on the device and the server.

parts.name: Cart screen
parts.what: Edit items, amounts and notes with the total always in view.

features.name: Delivery or pickup
features.does: Choose delivery to an address or pickup from the restaurant.

parts.name: Delivery or pickup choice
parts.what: Delivery, pickup, or the restaurant's own couriers, chosen per order.

parts.name: Pickup details
parts.what: Show where to collect, the opening hours and a pickup code.

features.name: Address and drop-off details
features.does: Enter an address, pin the exact door, and leave instructions such as a gate code.

parts.name: Drop-off pin
parts.what: Food's exact-door pin and drop-off checks on the kit's address search and address-from-a-pin.

parts.name: Drop-off instructions
parts.what: Notes, building, floor, gate code, and hand-to-me or leave-at-door.

parts.name: Saved addresses
parts.what: Home, work and others, with the last instructions remembered.

parts.name: Rural addresses
parts.what: Rural delivery numbers and road names matched to the official address data, with a map pin required wherever an address will not resolve.

features.name: Order ahead
features.does: Schedule an order for a set time later today or another day.

parts.name: Food lead times
parts.what: Food's rules for when a scheduled order goes to the kitchen, on the kit's scheduled bookings.

parts.name: Time slot picker
parts.what: Choose from times the restaurant and couriers can meet.

parts.name: Paying for orders days ahead
parts.what: Authorises the card close to cooking time because card holds expire, tells the customer in time if that fails, and invoices catering orders.

features.name: Clear price breakdown
features.does: See the full total, with every fee, before checkout begins, with menu prices including sales tax and nothing added later.

parts.name: Food price lines
parts.what: Food's price lines (menu total, delivery fee, platform fee and tip) on the kit's full-price-first calculator.

parts.name: Where-the-money-goes display
parts.what: Food's version of the kit's fee breakdown: what goes to the restaurant, the courier, the running cost and tax, with sales tax shown as included.

parts.name: Price display check
parts.what: Checks the price display against the consumer regulator's guidance on drip pricing (example: New Zealand's Commerce Commission): menu prices include sales tax, the full total appears before checkout, and sales tax reads as included, not added.

parts.name: Public holiday surcharge line
parts.what: A restaurant's public holiday surcharge as its own price line, shown on the restaurant card, the menu and the total before checkout on those days, never added at the end.

features.name: Pay
features.does: Pay by card or phone wallet, and save a method for next time.

parts.name: Food checkout
parts.what: The kit's shared checkout with Food's order summary, so Spareware never handles card numbers.

parts.name: Order placed confirmation
parts.what: Confirm the order, the hold on the money and the expected time.

features.name: Group orders
features.does: Share a cart link so friends add their own dishes, then split the bill or have one person pay.

parts.name: Shared cart
parts.what: A cart several people edit live, with each person's items marked.

parts.name: Bill splitting
parts.what: Each person pays their own share, or the host pays for everyone, through the payment provider.

parts.name: Group order screens
parts.what: Invite link, who has added what, and a lock-and-send button.

features.name: Change or cancel an order
features.does: Change or cancel an order before the kitchen starts, and see what a late cancel costs before confirming.

parts.name: Food cancel rules
parts.what: Food's change and cancel rules, such as free before the kitchen starts, as a policy on the kit's cancellation policies.

parts.name: Cancel flow
parts.what: A cancel button that shows the refund before confirming.

features.name: Notes and requests
features.does: Add a note for the kitchen and one for the courier, and say whether cutlery is wanted.

parts.name: Kitchen and courier notes
parts.what: Separate notes for each, with a cutlery and napkins switch that is off by default to cut waste.

features.name: Order as a gift
features.does: Send food to someone else's address with a message, and let them follow it.

parts.name: Gift order
parts.what: Recipient name, phone and message, with tracking shared with the recipient only once they agree.

parts.name: Refuse and block gift orders
parts.what: A recipient can refuse a gift order and block its sender, and senders face limits on sending food to addresses that are not their own.

features.name: Reusable packaging
features.does: Choose reusable containers where a local return scheme exists.

parts.name: Reusable container scheme research
parts.what: How existing reusable container schemes in each country work and whether they can link in, starting with New Zealand's.

features.name: Allergy request the kitchen must answer
features.does: A customer states an allergy on the order, and the kitchen must accept or decline it before cooking.

parts.name: Allergy request
parts.what: The allergens the customer must avoid, chosen from the same list as the dish fields, attached to the order.

parts.name: Kitchen allergy answer
parts.what: The order screen holds an order with an allergy request until the kitchen accepts or declines it; a decline cancels and refunds in full.

features.name: Access needs travel with the order
features.does: A customer's access needs, such as 'message, don't call' or 'bring it to the door', reach the courier and the restaurant on every order.

parts.name: Access needs
parts.what: Saved needs such as 'message, don't call', 'bring it to the door', a wheelchair user or a guide dog, kept with consent on the kit profile, which should hold access needs for every app, and attached to every order.

parts.name: Needs on the job
parts.what: Shows each party only the instruction it needs, such as 'bring it to the door' for the courier and never the reason, on the courier's offer and drop-off screens and the restaurant's pickup screen.

features.name: Order by phone call or text
features.does: A person without a smartphone or data orders by phone call or text, and gets status updates by text.

parts.name: Text ordering
parts.what: Food's text ordering from favourites or a past order, with status updates by text; an order on a saved card needs a PIN or an approval in the app, and texts go through the kit's text cost guard. The text channel itself should move down into the kit, since Spare Ride maps the same.

parts.name: Phone ordering line
parts.what: Food's phone ordering: a person takes the order into the same order path through the kit's phone support channels, including the national relay service (example: NZ Relay in New Zealand). The phone line itself should move down into the kit, since Spare Ride maps the same.

features.name: Order from several restaurants at once
features.does: A customer orders from two nearby restaurants in one checkout.

parts.name: Multi-restaurant cart
parts.what: One checkout split into one order per restaurant, sharing one courier only when both lie on one route.

features.name: Change where it goes
features.does: A customer changes the address after ordering, or has food brought to a place with no address, such as a park or a beach.

parts.name: Address change after ordering
parts.what: Changes the drop-off before pickup within a distance limit, showing any fee change first, and after pickup only with the courier's agreement.

parts.name: Drop-off at a place
parts.what: A map pin and a short meeting description for places with no address.

features.name: Past orders and receipts
features.does: A customer sees every past order with its receipt, reorders, and manages saved cards.

parts.name: Customer order history
parts.what: Food's past orders on the kit's orders page, with each receipt, the price lines and a reorder button.

parts.name: Saved cards
parts.what: The kit's saved payment methods in Food's checkout, holding only the provider's token and removable at any time.

features.name: Tell the restaurant you're here
features.does: A customer taps 'I'm here' on arrival, or asks for the order to be brought out to the car.

parts.name: I'm here and kerbside pickup
parts.what: An 'I'm here' button for pickup orders, and kerbside pickup where the restaurant offers it, with a note on where the car is, so disabled customers and parents with small children need not go inside.

features.name: Pay from your bank
features.does: A customer pays straight from their bank account once the payment provider supports it.

parts.name: Bank payment for food orders
parts.what: Turns on the kit's bank payments for Food once the payment provider supports them (moved here from FOOD-A4-F6-P2).

areas.name: Restaurant order handling
areas.summary: The restaurant's live screen: an order arrives with a sound, the kitchen accepts it and sets a time, marks it ready and hands it over.

features.name: Receive orders
features.does: A restaurant hears and sees each new order on a tablet, phone or computer, and accepts or declines it.

parts.name: Order screen
parts.what: A tablet-first app listing new, in-progress and ready orders.

parts.name: Loud alerts
parts.what: A repeating sound and screen flash until an order is accepted, even with the screen locked.

parts.name: Food order steps
parts.what: Food's steps on the kit's shared order steps and multi-party orders: received, accepted, preparing, ready, collected and delivered, plus declined, not accepted in time, cancelled by the customer, restaurant, courier or operator, undeliverable, returned, not collected for pickup orders, and part-refunded.

parts.name: Auto-accept
parts.what: Accept orders automatically when the restaurant chooses to.

parts.name: Rules for each unhappy step
parts.what: For each step that goes wrong, who is told, what is refunded, who bears the cost and what the courier is paid for work already done; an order not accepted in time is cancelled and refunded at once.

parts.name: Pickup not collected
parts.what: A paid pickup order nobody collects is held for a published time after it is ready, then marked not collected; the customer is told, the restaurant is paid, and the restaurant decides what happens to the food under its own food safety plan.

parts.name: Food that cannot be delivered
parts.what: A safe rule for food from cancelled, undeliverable or returned orders: never resold, returned to the restaurant or thrown away as the food rules study says, alcohol always returned to the seller, and the courier never charged for it.

features.name: Set and change prep times
features.does: A restaurant sets how long an order will take, and adds time when the kitchen is slammed.

parts.name: Prep time buttons
parts.what: Quick buttons to set a time or add minutes to an order.

parts.name: Prep time learning
parts.what: Learn each restaurant's real prep times by dish, time of day and queue length.

features.name: Mark ready and hand over
features.does: A restaurant marks an order ready and confirms the right courier or customer took it.

parts.name: Ready and collected buttons
parts.what: Mark ready, then confirm the hand-over.

parts.name: Hand-over code rules
parts.what: When Food asks for a hand-over code at the counter, on the kit's proof of handover, with a limit on wrong guesses.

parts.name: Courier arriving
parts.what: The order screen shows the assigned courier's first name, photo and vehicle from assignment to hand-over, a live arrival time, and 'courier waiting' once they reach the counter, so the kitchen times the food and staff hand the bag to the right person.

features.name: Pause and busy mode
features.does: A restaurant can pause new orders, close early, or add time to every order when busy.

parts.name: Pause, hours and holidays
parts.what: Pause for a set time, set regular hours and holiday closures.

parts.name: Busy mode
parts.what: Add minutes to every new order and shrink the delivery area while busy.

features.name: Item runs out mid-order
features.does: A restaurant tells the customer an item has run out and offers a swap or a refund.

parts.name: Swap or refund request
parts.what: The kitchen picks the missing item, and the customer approves a swap or a part refund in the app, on the kit's order changes.

features.name: Kitchen printing
features.does: A restaurant prints order tickets and bag labels on the kitchen printer it already has.

parts.name: Receipt printer support
parts.what: Print to common network and Bluetooth receipt printers using their published command sets.

parts.name: Bag labels
parts.what: A label with the order number and name for each bag.

features.name: Orders straight into the till
features.does: Orders go straight into the restaurant's point-of-sale system so staff never retype them.

parts.name: Point-of-sale order connectors
parts.what: Plugins that send orders into point-of-sale systems with open, licensable interfaces.

features.name: Order history and lookup
features.does: A restaurant can find any past order and see everything that happened to it.

parts.name: Restaurant order history
parts.what: Food's search fields and event detail on the kit's orders page.

features.name: Restaurant's own couriers
features.does: A restaurant delivers with its own staff and still uses the app for tracking and payment.

parts.name: Own-courier mode
parts.what: Assign the order to the restaurant's own courier accounts, with tracking and no courier fee taken.

features.name: Many locations
features.does: A restaurant group watches orders and pauses across all its locations from one screen.

parts.name: Multi-location view
parts.what: A live view of every location's orders, pauses and prep times.

features.name: Fallback when a restaurant goes silent
features.does: When a restaurant's device stops answering, the restaurant is paused and phoned or texted with the order, and the customer is refunded if nobody answers.

parts.name: Silence detection
parts.what: Spots a restaurant device that has stopped checking in during open hours, and pauses new orders.

parts.name: Call or text the restaurant
parts.what: An automatic call or text to the restaurant's phone with the waiting order, which staff can accept by reply.

parts.name: Cancel and refund on no answer
parts.what: Cancels and refunds in full if there is still no answer after a set time, and tells the customer straight away.

features.name: Order limits
features.does: A restaurant caps how many orders it takes in each 15 minutes, and sets a minimum order.

parts.name: Order cap
parts.what: The most orders a restaurant takes in each 15 minutes; once it is reached, new orders get a later time or wait for the next slot.

parts.name: Restaurant minimum order
parts.what: A minimum order value set by the restaurant, shown on its card and page before anything goes in the cart.

areas.name: Courier work
areas.summary: The courier's app: go online, see the full pay and distance before accepting, collect, deliver and get paid daily.

features.name: Go online and offline
features.does: A courier starts and stops work whenever they choose, with no penalty.

parts.name: Food availability rules
parts.what: Food's courier states (online, offline and on a job) on the kit's worker availability.

parts.name: Courier home screen
parts.what: Go-online button, today's earnings and how busy it is nearby.

parts.name: Visa hour limits
parts.what: Stops offers once a courier reaches the weekly hours their visa allows, counted across every Spareware app, wherever the status decision makes that limit apply.

parts.name: Hours across Spareware apps
parts.what: Counts a courier's online and engaged hours across every Spareware app, not only Food, for visa limits, fatigue limits and minimum pay; it reads the kit's worker availability, which should keep this as one shared worker record, since Spare Ride relies on it too.

features.name: See the whole offer first
features.does: A courier sees the pay, pickup, drop-off area and distance before accepting, and can decline with no penalty.

parts.name: Job offer card
parts.what: Food's offer details on the kit's job offer screen: pay, any checkout tip (which can then never be cut), pickup, a rough drop-off area from the kit's approximate location, distance, time and the restaurant's pickup notes.

parts.name: Offer timeout
parts.what: Food's offer time limit on the kit's dispatch engine, long enough to read safely before the offer passes on.

parts.name: No-penalty rule
parts.what: Acceptance rates are never used to punish, written into Food's rules on the kit's fair offer rules.

features.name: Navigate
features.does: A courier gets directions suited to a bike, e-bike, scooter, car or walking.

parts.name: Vehicle routing profiles
parts.what: Food's bike, e-bike, scooter, car and walking profiles on the kit's routing service.

parts.name: Directions hand-off
parts.what: Hands the route to the courier's own map app at first, and to the kit's turn-by-turn guidance once that is built.

features.name: Pickup and drop-off
features.does: A courier confirms pickup with the order code, and drop-off by hand-over, photo or code.

parts.name: Pickup check
parts.what: Check the code and the number of bags, and log any wait.

parts.name: Food proof of delivery
parts.what: Food's rules on the kit's proof of handover: a leave-at-door photo that frames only the door, blurs any people and is kept a short time only, or a code for valuable and age-restricted orders.

parts.name: Customer not there
parts.what: Call, wait on a timer, then leave or return as the published rules say.

parts.name: Faked location checks
parts.what: Food's waiting pay, distance pay and proof of delivery use the kit's faked location checks, so a spoofed position is flagged for a person before pay or a delivery claim relies on it.

parts.name: Pickup notes for couriers
parts.what: A restaurant's notes for couriers on where to park, which door to use and whether couriers may use the toilet, shown on the offer and the pickup screen.

features.name: Two orders at once
features.does: A courier can carry two orders going the same way, with the extra pay shown before accepting.

parts.name: Batched job display
parts.what: Both drop-offs, the order to deliver them in, and the combined pay.

features.name: Earnings and payouts
features.does: A courier sees every job's pay, tips and fees, and is paid daily.

parts.name: Food earnings view
parts.what: Food's earnings lines (delivery fees, waiting pay and tips) on the kit's earnings page.

parts.name: Daily payout
parts.what: Food couriers are paid daily on the kit's payout runs, at no extra charge where the provider allows.

parts.name: Tax statements
parts.what: Food's figures (delivery fees, tips and sales tax) on the kit's yearly statements.

parts.name: Mileage and expense log
parts.what: Food's work kilometres from finished jobs, without keeping the route, and expenses with a receipt photo, for a year-end tax pack. The log itself should move down into the kit, since Spare Ride maps the same.

parts.name: Pay for wasted trips
parts.what: A courier who accepted a job that is then cancelled, undeliverable or returned is paid for the distance and time already worked, at the voted rate, with the cost falling where the unhappy-step rules say.

features.name: Paid for waiting
features.does: A courier is paid for waiting at a restaurant beyond the ready time.

parts.name: Waiting time pay
parts.what: Measure time from arrival to hand-over and pay it at the voted rate.

features.name: Busy times and booked shifts
features.does: A courier sees when and where it gets busy, and can book a block of time if members choose to offer that.

parts.name: Food demand view
parts.what: Food's busy times and areas on the kit's demand maps.

parts.name: Optional shift booking
parts.what: Book blocks of time with a guaranteed hourly minimum, if members vote for it.

features.name: Vehicle and gear
features.does: A courier sets their vehicle, and is only offered jobs that suit it, such as no large catering orders on a bike.

parts.name: Vehicle profile
parts.what: Vehicle type, carrying space and insulated bag.

parts.name: Jobs a courier won't carry
parts.what: A courier can opt out of alcohol jobs, and of other restricted goods once they exist, for any reason including religion, and is then never offered them or penalised for it.

features.name: Keep working without signal
features.does: A courier can carry on a job through a dead zone, and the app catches up when signal returns.

parts.name: Offline job steps
parts.what: Food's courier job steps queued on the phone and replayed in order by the kit's sync engine.

features.name: Both apps, one courier
features.does: A courier can take Spare Food jobs and other Spareware jobs, such as rides, from one account, if they choose.

parts.name: Shared availability
parts.what: Food's offers join the kit's one worker availability, which serves every Spareware app; Food holds only its own clash rules, such as no Food offer while a courier is on a ride.

features.name: Safe to use while moving
features.does: A courier never needs to type or tap while moving: offers are read aloud and the screen suits a phone cradle.

parts.name: Driving-safe mode
parts.what: Food's courier screens in a driving-safe mode: no typing or taps while moving, large targets, and offers read aloud, shown large and signalled by vibration. The mode itself should move down into the kit, since Spare Ride maps the same.

parts.name: Safe offer timing
parts.what: Offer time limits long enough to pull over, and one large button to accept, so nobody taps fast while moving.

parts.name: Phone rules on the road
parts.what: What each country's road rules allow for phones in cradles on bikes, e-bikes, scooters and in cars, starting with New Zealand's. This research should be shared through the kit, since Spare Ride needs the car case.

features.name: Pay the law requires for the courier's status
features.does: A courier is paid at least what the law requires for their status, with the records, breaks and leave an employee is owed if couriers are employees.

parts.name: Minimum pay per engaged hour
parts.what: Food's engaged time, from accepting an offer to drop-off including waits, and its earnings fed to the kit's minimum pay top-up, wherever the status decision or a member vote applies it.

parts.name: Shifts and hourly pay for employees
parts.what: If couriers are employees: rostered shifts, hourly pay for all time on shift, and jobs offered within a shift by the same published rules.

parts.name: Wage and time records
parts.what: The wage, time, holiday and leave records employment law requires for employee couriers, kept from Food's shift and job records for as long as the law says.

parts.name: Rest and meal breaks
parts.what: Rest and meal breaks for employee couriers as employment law requires (example: New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000), with offers paused during each break.

parts.name: Holidays and leave
parts.what: Holiday pay, public holiday pay and sick leave for employee couriers, on the kit's holiday pay.

parts.name: Payroll, income tax and retirement savings (example: New Zealand's PAYE and KiwiSaver)
parts.what: Employee couriers paid through the kit's payroll provider link, which handles income tax, retirement savings and payday filing (example: PAYE and KiwiSaver in New Zealand), with the kit's guidance for each status on the earnings page.

parts.name: Union access and bargaining
parts.what: What the co-op owes as an employer if couriers are employees: union access, good-faith bargaining, and how a collective agreement sits with member votes on pay (example: New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000). The kit should hold this rule for every app.

areas.name: Dispatch and timing
areas.summary: The engine that sends the right courier so they arrive as the food is ready, not before, and keeps every time estimate honest.

features.name: Courier arrives as the food is ready
features.does: A courier is offered a job at the ready time minus their travel time, so food and couriers wait as little as possible.

parts.name: Ready-time estimate
parts.what: Combine the restaurant's set time with its learned prep times.

parts.name: Food travel times
parts.what: Courier-to-restaurant travel time for each vehicle type, from the kit's routing service and arrival time estimates.

parts.name: Food dispatch rules
parts.what: Food's scoring rules for the shared matching engine: distance, ready time, vehicle fit and fair sharing.

features.name: Honest delivery times
features.does: A customer sees a delivery time that holds up, and that updates as the order moves.

parts.name: Delivery time model
parts.what: Predict total time from prep, courier arrival and the ride to the door.

parts.name: Accuracy tracking
parts.what: Measures each estimate against the real time and publishes how accurate it was as open data.

parts.name: Late order remedy
parts.what: A published remedy when an order arrives much later than the time shown at checkout, such as a part refund within limits members vote on, paid by whoever caused the delay under the who-pays rules, or from the reserve when nobody did, and never taken from the courier's fee.

features.name: Batching
features.does: Two orders going the same way share one courier when neither ends up late.

parts.name: Food batching limits
parts.what: Food's lateness limit, set by members, on the kit's batching.

features.name: Reassignment
features.does: If a courier drops a job or is held up, it passes quickly to another courier.

parts.name: Stalled job detection and re-offer
parts.what: Spot a stalled job and offer it again with the food's ready state.

features.name: Fair job sharing
features.does: Jobs are shared fairly between online couriers by rules members can read and vote on.

parts.name: Published dispatch rules
parts.what: A plain-English description of how jobs are given out, kept in step with the code.

parts.name: Fairness measures
parts.what: Food's measures, such as earnings per online hour across couriers, on the kit's fairness checks.

parts.name: Customer ratings and fair areas
parts.what: Decides whether couriers see a customer's rating before accepting, and tests that dispatch serves every area and group fairly.

features.name: Busy-time forecasts
features.does: The co-op can see busy times coming so enough couriers are online.

parts.name: Demand forecast
parts.what: Forecast orders by area and hour from past orders, events and weather.

features.name: Zones and delivery distance
features.does: Operators set where the service runs and how far each restaurant delivers.

parts.name: Food zones
parts.what: Food's service areas drawn and edited on the kit's service areas.

parts.name: Delivery distance rules
parts.what: Distance limits per restaurant and per zone, tightened automatically when couriers are short.

areas.name: Live tracking and messages
areas.summary: Everyone can see where the order is up to and talk to each other without sharing phone numbers.

features.name: Live order status
features.does: A customer sees each step from accepted to delivered, on screen and in notifications.

parts.name: Status timeline
parts.what: Food's order steps and times on the kit's order timeline.

parts.name: Status notifications
parts.what: Food's status messages sent by push, text or email through the kit's notification router.

parts.name: Lock-screen live status
parts.what: Live status on the phone's lock screen, where the phone allows it.

features.name: Courier on the map
features.does: A customer sees the courier moving on a map once the food is collected, and not before.

parts.name: Courier location during delivery
parts.what: Shares the courier's position on the kit's live location stream only from collection to drop-off, not kept afterwards, with a trace only where the law, safety or a dispute needs it.

parts.name: Tracking map
parts.what: A map showing the courier, the route and the drop-off.

features.name: Messages and calls
features.does: Customer, courier and restaurant can message or call each other through masked numbers.

parts.name: Order chat
parts.what: A Food chat for each order on the kit's chat service, closed after delivery and kept for disputes.

parts.name: Masked calling
parts.what: Food turns on the kit's masked calls for each order until it is delivered.

parts.name: Quick replies
parts.what: Food's ready-made messages, such as 'on my way' and 'at the door', on the kit's chat screens, translated for the reader.

features.name: Share tracking
features.does: A customer can share a tracking link with someone else.

parts.name: Tracking link
parts.what: Food's shared tracking link on the kit's trusted contact link, showing the status only, not the courier's details.

features.name: Lateness alerts
features.does: A customer is told early if an order will be late, and why.

parts.name: Delay detection
parts.what: Spot when the estimate slips past a limit and send the reason.

areas.name: Pricing, fees and deals
areas.summary: How the price is set: the menu price, a delivery fee the couriers vote on, the at-cost platform fee, and optional tips and deals.

features.name: Delivery fee by distance and time
features.does: A customer pays a delivery fee set by distance and time, and all of it goes to the courier.

parts.name: Delivery fee formula
parts.what: A formula by distance, time and waiting, with a published minimum, set by courier vote only in a form the competition law check clears.

parts.name: Fee history
parts.what: Every past formula and when it changed, published.

features.name: At-cost platform fee
features.does: A customer and a restaurant see the platform fee, last period's running cost divided by orders, and who pays it, on every order.

parts.name: Food fee rate
parts.what: Food's fee per order from the kit's fee calculator and fee setting, with pickup and delivery rates apart, the first period's fee from the start-up rule, and sales tax on the fee where it applies.

parts.name: Pickup fee rule
parts.what: Pickup orders pay only the payment provider's charge.

parts.name: What the fee may cover
parts.what: A decision, put to members, on which costs the at-cost fee may cover: support workers, operators, panel pay, translators, legal advice, insurance, marketing, a reserve and paying for the build itself.

parts.name: Who pays the fee
parts.what: Decides whether the customer, the restaurant or both pay the platform fee, before the price calculator is built.

parts.name: Food's card surcharge cases
parts.what: Food's pickup and pay-at-table orders put to the kit's card fee pass-through check, so passing payment charges through stays lawful once the planned in-store surcharge ban applies.

parts.name: First-period fee
parts.what: Food's first fee, when there is no last period, set from the kit's launch cost estimate and Food's expected orders by the kit's start-up fee rule, then trued up once real costs are known.

features.name: Tips
features.does: A customer can tip the courier before or after delivery, the courier gets all of it, and a tip the courier saw before accepting is never cut.

parts.name: Tip flow
parts.what: Food's tip timing on the kit's tips: a tip set at checkout shows on the courier's offer and can only go up once a courier accepts; after delivery a customer can add or raise a tip for a set time, but never lower one.

features.name: Small-order and busy-time rules
features.does: Members can choose a small-order fee or a busy-time courier bonus, always shown before the order.

parts.name: Small-order fee
parts.what: An optional fee below a set order value, voted by members.

parts.name: Busy-time bonus
parts.what: A courier bonus at busy times, paid from a fee shown to the customer.

features.name: Restaurant deals
features.does: A restaurant can run its own discounts, such as free delivery or a dish deal, paid for by the restaurant.

parts.name: Food deal kinds
parts.what: Food's deal kinds (free delivery, dish deals and free items) on the kit's promotions and vouchers, always paid for by the restaurant, so the courier still gets the whole delivery fee.

parts.name: Deal set-up screen
parts.what: Create a deal and see how it performed in the restaurant app.

features.name: Promo codes and referrals
features.does: A customer can use a promo code, and invite friends for credit.

parts.name: Promo codes
parts.what: Codes with limits, paid for by a restaurant, or from the fee only if members vote to include marketing in it.

parts.name: Referral credit
parts.what: Invite links with credit paid for by a restaurant, or from the fee only if members vote for it, with limits to stop abuse.

features.name: Gift cards and credit
features.does: A customer can buy a gift card, and can choose credit instead of money back when refunded.

parts.name: Food gift cards
parts.what: Food gift cards on the kit's gift cards, held and settled by the payment provider.

features.name: Member benefits instead of subscriptions
features.does: A customer could get lower fees as a free member instead of through a paid subscription, if members vote for it.

parts.name: Customer member benefits question
parts.what: What customers who take part as members would get, put to a vote.

areas.name: Payments, payouts and tax
areas.summary: The money: held by a regulated payment provider, split between the restaurant, the courier, the at-cost fee, sales tax and the provider's charge, paid out daily, and taxed as each country's law requires.

features.name: Pay and hold
features.does: A customer's payment is approved when they order and taken on hand-over, held all the while by the payment provider.

parts.name: Hold and capture
parts.what: Food's timing on the kit's hold and release rules: approve at order, and take the money at collection or delivery.

parts.name: Failed payment handling
parts.what: Retry, ask for another method, or cancel before the kitchen starts.

features.name: Order money split
features.does: Each order's money splits automatically between the restaurant, the courier, the at-cost fee, the sales tax the platform collects and the payment provider's charge.

parts.name: Split rules
parts.what: Food's split on the kit's multi-party orders: the restaurant gets the menu total less its own deals, the courier the delivery fee and tips, and the fee, the sales tax for the tax office and the provider's charge each get their own line.

parts.name: Split record
parts.what: Every split stored as operations linked to the order, so payouts, sales tax and the kit's reconciliation agree.

features.name: Payouts
features.does: Restaurants and couriers are paid daily, with every deduction shown.

parts.name: Food payout timing
parts.what: Daily payouts to restaurants and couriers on the kit's payout runs.

parts.name: Payout statements
parts.what: Food's statement lines (orders, fees, refunds and tips) on the kit's earnings page and receipts.

features.name: Sales tax on the listed service (example: New Zealand GST)
features.does: The platform collects sales tax on food delivery where the law makes the platform collect it (example: New Zealand GST on listed services), and gives sellers what the law says they need.

parts.name: What counts as the listed service
parts.what: Which parts of a food order the marketplace rules cover, and how restaurants' own sales tax fits, using the seller of record decision.

parts.name: Food sales tax rules
parts.what: Food's sales tax rules for each order line on the kit's sales tax engine, including flat-rate credit notices to unregistered restaurants and couriers.

parts.name: Food lines for sales tax returns
parts.what: Food's order lines in the kit's operator sales tax returns.

parts.name: Tax invoices
parts.what: Tax invoices for customers and business accounts, invoices to restaurants and couriers for the platform fee they pay, and buyer-created tax invoices where the platform issues them for couriers, on the kit's tax invoices.

features.name: Income reporting to the tax office (example: New Zealand's IRD)
features.does: The platform reports sellers' income as the digital platform rules require.

parts.name: Food income reporting
parts.what: Food's seller details for couriers, and for restaurants if the rules cover them, on the kit's yearly report to the tax office.

features.name: Refunds
features.does: A customer gets a refund quickly, and its cost falls on whoever caused the problem.

parts.name: Food refund rules
parts.what: Food's refund cases and who bears each cost, on the kit's refunds.

parts.name: Money back by default
parts.what: Every refund goes back the way the customer paid unless they choose credit, and credit is never the only choice, as consumer law requires (example: New Zealand's Consumer Guarantees Act).

features.name: Bank chargebacks
features.does: The co-op can answer a bank chargeback with the order's evidence.

parts.name: Food chargeback evidence
parts.what: The order events, photos and messages Food adds to the kit's card dispute answers.

features.name: Anti-money-laundering duties
features.does: The co-op meets the anti-money-laundering rules for online marketplaces.

parts.name: Food money-laundering risks
parts.what: Food's own risks, such as people ordering from themselves to move money, fed into the kit's anti-money-laundering programme.

parts.name: Suspicious pattern checks
parts.what: Flag patterns such as people ordering from themselves to move money.

parts.name: Checks on restaurants and couriers
parts.what: The customer checks the programme requires for restaurants and couriers, run through the kit's customer checks with the identity and payment providers.

parts.name: Sanctions screening
parts.what: Restaurants and couriers screened against sanctions lists through the kit's sanctions screening before their first payout.

features.name: Cash on pickup
features.does: A restaurant can take cash for pickup orders if members choose to allow it.

parts.name: Cash order record
parts.what: Record cash orders outside the payment provider and invoice the fee.

features.name: Debts and negative balances
features.does: A restaurant or courier whose refunds or fees exceed their next payout sees the debt, how it will be recovered and the limits on recovery.

parts.name: Negative balance rules
parts.what: Food's limits on the kit's negative balances: which Food refunds and fees can create a debt, the most taken from one payout, and when a role is paused.

parts.name: Leaving while owing
parts.what: Food's steps when someone leaves owing money, on the kit's loss rules: a payment plan, no hidden penalties, and recovery only by lawful means.

features.name: Tax set aside from payouts
features.does: A courier chooses a rate of tax to be held back from each payout, so the year-end bill is no shock.

parts.name: Voluntary withholding with the tax office (example: New Zealand's IRD)
parts.what: Confirms with the tax office how voluntary withholding works when a platform pays a courier, starting with New Zealand's IRD. The rule should move down into the kit, since Spare Work maps the same.

parts.name: Withholding from payouts
parts.what: Holds back the courier's chosen rate from each payout on the kit's payout runs and shows it on the statement. The withholding itself should move down into the kit with the rule.

features.name: Safe payout changes
features.does: A restaurant's or courier's payout account cannot be quietly redirected after an account takeover.

parts.name: Food payout change rules
parts.what: Food's use of the kit's payout change guard for restaurant owners and couriers, with Food's waiting time before money goes to a new account.

parts.name: Two-person approval
parts.what: Staff overrides and large manual refunds need a second person to approve them.

features.name: Warning before the sales tax threshold
features.does: A courier or a small restaurant is told when its sales near the sales tax registration threshold, and what registering would change.

parts.name: Sales tax threshold warning
parts.what: Warns a courier or an unregistered restaurant as its sales in every Spareware app near the country's sales tax registration threshold (example: $60,000 for New Zealand GST), and explains what registering changes for flat-rate credits and invoices. How platform sales count towards the threshold is for the sales tax study to confirm (*unverified*), and the warning should move down into the kit, since Spare Ride and Spare Work need it.

areas.name: Support, refunds and disputes
areas.summary: When something goes wrong: report it in a few taps, get a fair answer fast, and appeal to a member panel.

features.name: Help centre
features.does: A person can find answers to common problems in their own language.

parts.name: Help articles
parts.what: Food's plain-language help for customers, restaurants and couriers, in the kit's help centre.

parts.name: Help inside the app
parts.what: Food's help links on each order screen into the kit's help centre.

features.name: Report a problem with an order
features.does: A customer reports missing, wrong, cold, spilled or late food with photos, and small claims are refunded in minutes.

parts.name: Problem report flow
parts.what: Pick the order, the items and the problem, and add photos; sickness or an allergic reaction goes to the urgent path.

parts.name: Instant refund rules
parts.what: Small claims refunded at once within published limits; larger ones go to a person.

parts.name: Who pays rules
parts.what: Decide whether the restaurant, the courier, the platform or nobody bears the cost, by published rules.

features.name: Talk to a person
features.does: A person can chat with a support worker about a live order, and a courier gets urgent help on the road.

parts.name: Food support cases
parts.what: Food's case types and order history views in the kit's support console.

parts.name: Support chat
parts.what: Chat with a support worker from the order, on the kit's chat and support cases.

parts.name: Courier urgent line
parts.what: Food's urgent cases for couriers mid-job, such as a closed restaurant or a crash, on the kit's urgent support routing.

parts.name: Published support levels
parts.what: Support hours and response times, a phone line for restaurants during service, and the languages covered, published and measured.

features.name: Disputes and member panels
features.does: A restaurant, courier or customer can dispute a decision, and the money stays held until a member panel decides.

parts.name: Food dispute types
parts.what: Food's dispute categories and the payouts each one holds, on the kit's disputes service.

parts.name: Food panels
parts.what: Food panels on the kit's panel selection and workspace, balanced for each case: a customer's claim against a restaurant or a courier is never heard by a panel drawn only from the side complained about, and outcomes are published without names.

parts.name: Appeals
parts.what: Food decisions go to the kit's appeals, with written reasons.

parts.name: Settle first
parts.what: Every dispute starts with a settlement offer through the kit's settlement offers and dispute clocks, and claims under a published amount are settled by the refund rules, never sent to a panel.

features.name: Consumer law
features.does: Customers get what consumer law promises (example: New Zealand's Consumer Guarantees Act and Fair Trading Act).

parts.name: Consumer law study
parts.what: Who owes which guarantee when a restaurant, a courier and a platform share one order.

parts.name: Seller of record for each order
parts.what: Food's case for the kit's seller of record decision: the restaurant sells the meal, and the courier or the co-op sells the delivery, which sets who charges sales tax, who owes consumer guarantees, whose name is on each receipt and who answers card disputes.

features.name: False claims
features.does: Repeated false claims are spotted and handled fairly, with a person always deciding.

parts.name: Claim pattern checks
parts.what: Patterns across customers, couriers and restaurants, flagged for a person to review.

features.name: Report sickness or an allergic reaction
features.does: A customer reports food sickness or an allergic reaction, a person acts on it at once, and the restaurant is told and paused when a pattern or the law calls for it.

parts.name: Sickness and reaction report
parts.what: A separate, urgent report for illness or an allergic reaction, which first tells the person to call the emergency number or a health line if they need care (example: 111 or Healthline in New Zealand).

parts.name: Urgent triage
parts.what: A person reviews every sickness or reaction report straight away, at any hour.

parts.name: Evidence freeze
parts.what: The order, the dish details, photos and chat are frozen as soon as a report is made.

parts.name: Restaurant notice and pause
parts.what: Tells the restaurant, and pauses it when reports form a pattern or a council closes it.

parts.name: Telling the food regulator and councils
parts.what: When the law asks the restaurant or the platform to tell the food safety regulator (example: New Zealand's MPI) or the council, and how the platform helps.

features.name: Take it further
features.does: A customer, restaurant or courier learns how to take a dispute to a small claims tribunal (example: New Zealand's Disputes Tribunal) or another outside route.

parts.name: Outside routes for Food
parts.what: Food's links to small claims tribunals and other outside routes, on the kit's guidance.

features.name: AI help with limits
features.does: A person gets quick answers from an AI helper that says it is an AI and hands over to a person whenever asked.

parts.name: AI helper limits
parts.what: The kit's help assistant answers Food questions first, says it is an AI, hands over to a person on request, and cannot go past refund limits.

areas.name: Ratings, trust and safety
areas.summary: Two-way ratings, safety tools for couriers and customers, and checks that keep bad actors out, with every decision logged in public.

features.name: Two-way ratings
features.does: A customer rates the food and the delivery separately, and couriers, restaurants and customers rate each other.

parts.name: Separate food and delivery ratings
parts.what: Food's two rating subjects (the food and the delivery) on the kit's ratings, so nobody is blamed for the other's mistake.

parts.name: Customer ratings
parts.what: Couriers and restaurants rate customers, and customers can see their own rating.

parts.name: Couriers and restaurants rate each other
parts.what: Couriers rate restaurants on waits, packing and hand-over, and restaurants rate couriers, feeding the quality report and waiting pay.

parts.name: Challenge a rating
parts.what: A courier, restaurant or customer challenges a single unfair rating with the order's facts, through the kit's rating challenge.

features.name: Reviews
features.does: A customer can write a review, and the restaurant can reply in public.

parts.name: Review and reply
parts.what: Food's review fields (food, packing and delivery) on the kit's reviews, with the restaurant's public reply.

parts.name: Review moderation
parts.what: Food's review rules on the kit's moderation queue and fair review rules, including how defamation complaints about reviews are handled, with each removal logged.

parts.name: Fake review checks
parts.what: Food's signs of review rings and attacks by rival restaurants, such as orders placed only to leave a review, on the kit's fake review checks, for a person to review.

features.name: Fair removal
features.does: No courier or restaurant is removed by an algorithm alone: they get a reason, a chance to answer and an appeal.

parts.name: Food removal steps
parts.what: Food's warnings and rating levels on the kit's rating thresholds and statements of reasons, with review by a person and an appeal to a member panel.

features.name: Courier safety tools
features.does: A courier can call for help, share their job with someone and report unsafe places, under a health and safety plan.

parts.name: Emergency button
parts.what: The kit's emergency button on every courier and customer job screen.

parts.name: Trip sharing
parts.what: A courier shares the live job with a trusted contact through the kit's trusted contact link.

parts.name: Incident reports
parts.what: Food's incident types on the kit's incident register and reports service: crashes, injuries, near misses, dog attacks, threats, harassment, and sexual harm, which goes only to the sexual harm path, with follow-up from a person.

parts.name: Food's health and safety facts
parts.what: Food's facts for the kit's health and safety duties: riding and driving at night, doorstep encounters, carrying hot or heavy orders, and severe weather.

parts.name: Health and safety plan
parts.what: The co-op's plan for courier fatigue, violence, severe weather and crashes, as a business owing health and safety duties.

parts.name: Fatigue limits
parts.what: Food's limits on the kit's work-time limits: nudges after long hours online, and a voted limit on hours in a day, counted across every Spareware app.

parts.name: Workplace safety notices
parts.what: Flags Food incidents that must be notified to the workplace safety regulator (example: New Zealand's WorkSafe), such as a death or a serious injury in a crash, and tracks the notice and keeping the scene as it was, on the kit's notifiable event reports.

parts.name: After violence or a crash
parts.what: Food's steps after a courier is assaulted or crashes mid-job, on the kit's violence and crash handling: safety first, the order passed on or written off at no cost to the courier, support, the incident record and insurance.

features.name: Fraud and account safety
features.does: The platform spots stolen cards, fake accounts and shared courier accounts.

parts.name: Fraud signals
parts.what: Food's fraud rules (new devices, mismatched addresses and card testing) on the kit's fraud signals and the provider's screening.

parts.name: Courier identity re-check
parts.what: Food's re-check timing, such as the start of some shifts, on the kit's repeat face checks, which bring the fairness testing, the non-biometric option and a person reviewing every failure.

features.name: Food safe in transit
features.does: Food arrives safe: sealed bags, insulated gear and published rules for couriers.

parts.name: Tamper-evident seals
parts.what: Seal guidance for restaurants and a prompt for customers to check the seal.

parts.name: Food in transit rules
parts.what: What couriers must do to keep food safe and suitable on the way.

features.name: Public moderation log
features.does: Anyone can see each removal or ban and the rule behind it, without names.

parts.name: Moderation log
parts.what: Food's trust decisions published through the kit's public removal log.

features.name: Customer safety
features.does: A customer can report a courier or restaurant for unsafe behaviour and block them from future orders.

parts.name: Report and block
parts.what: Report a person from the order and block them through the kit's blocking, so they are never matched again.

features.name: Insurance in place
features.does: Couriers, customers and the co-op are covered by insurance that is bought, not just studied.

parts.name: Co-op cover
parts.what: Third-party liability and property damage cover for couriers on bikes, scooters and cars, bought before launch.

parts.name: Car policy check
parts.what: A courier on a car confirms their own policy covers delivery work, recorded as a check result.

parts.name: Income cover beyond public accident cover
parts.what: Options for income cover beyond public accident cover (example: New Zealand's ACC), such as a co-op group policy.

parts.name: Crash report and claim
parts.what: A courier reports a crash with photos and details, and starts the insurance claim, through the kit's violence and crash handling and insurance claims link.

features.name: Warnings about unsafe addresses
features.does: A courier sees hazard notes on an address, such as a dog, steep steps or an unsafe entry, before accepting.

parts.name: Address hazard notes
parts.what: Couriers add hazard notes to an address, shown on later offers to that address, on the kit's hazard notes; notes describe the place, never the people.

features.name: Report sexual harm safely
features.does: A courier, customer or restaurant worker reports sexual harm from any order and is looked after by trained responders.

parts.name: Food's sexual harm path
parts.what: Every Food report screen and the emergency button lead to the kit's sexual harm path, handled only by trained responders, with the reporter choosing whether police are told and the two people never matched again.

features.name: Treated fairly whoever you are
features.does: Couriers, customers and restaurant staff all agree not to refuse or treat anyone worse because of who they are.

parts.name: Food's non-discrimination rules
parts.what: The kit's non-discrimination commitment, accepted at sign-up by couriers, customers and restaurant staff, with Food's examples, such as never refusing an order or a courier because of a name, a religion or a race.

features.name: Checks for unfair declines
features.does: Patterns of declines and cancels that point to discrimination are spotted for a person to review.

parts.name: Food decline pattern checks
parts.what: Declines and cancels by couriers and restaurants fed to the kit's decline pattern checks, for a person to review, never for automatic penalties.

features.name: Report a courier on the road
features.does: Anyone, with or without an account, can report a courier's riding or driving.

parts.name: Public road report
parts.what: A web form with no sign-in that takes the place, the time and a short code shown on the courier's bag, which says nothing about the courier, matched to the job by the kit's reports service, with spam limits and the courier's name never shown to the reporter.

areas.name: Restaurant business tools
areas.summary: What a restaurant needs to run its delivery trade: reports, payouts, feedback, help, and its own ordering link at the same at-cost fee.

features.name: Sales and payout reports
features.does: A restaurant sees sales, fees, refunds and payouts by day, week and month, and downloads them.

parts.name: Sales dashboard
parts.what: Orders, sales, fees and refunds with simple charts.

parts.name: Accounting export
parts.what: Food's sales and fee lines in the kit's accounting exports.

features.name: Menu performance
features.does: A restaurant sees which dishes sell, when they sell out and what each one earns.

parts.name: Dish insights
parts.what: Orders, sales and sold-out time for each dish; ratings and complaints stay in the quality report.

features.name: Order quality feedback
features.does: A restaurant sees its ratings, complaints and accuracy, by dish and over time, and what to fix first.

parts.name: Quality report
parts.what: Missing-item rate, prep-time accuracy, complaints and ratings by dish and over time, including couriers' ratings of waits and packing.

features.name: Own ordering link
features.does: A restaurant shares a link or QR code so customers order straight from its own website, at the same at-cost fee.

parts.name: Direct ordering page
parts.what: A simple page in the restaurant's own colours and logo that uses the same menu and checkout, on a shared shop page the kit should open now, since Spare Market needs one too.

parts.name: QR code and website embed
parts.what: QR codes and a website embed for the ordering page.

features.name: Order at the table
features.does: A diner scans a code at the table and orders and pays from their phone.

parts.name: Table ordering mode
parts.what: Table number on the order and pay-at-table through the same checkout, on a shared till the kit should open, since Spare Market needs one too.

features.name: Message followers
features.does: A restaurant can tell customers who chose to follow it about a new menu, without paying for ads.

parts.name: Follower messages
parts.what: Messages only to customers who opted in, within the anti-spam law.

features.name: Monthly tax summary
features.does: A restaurant gets the sales tax and income figures it needs each month.

parts.name: Tax summary
parts.what: Sales, sales tax handled by the platform, and fees for each month.

features.name: Set-up help and test orders
features.does: A restaurant learns the app quickly and can send a test order before going live.

parts.name: Set-up guide
parts.what: Step-by-step set-up with checks for menu, hours and payouts.

parts.name: Test order mode
parts.what: Run a test order through the whole flow without charging anyone.

areas.name: More than restaurant meals
areas.summary: The other things the big apps deliver: groceries and convenience goods, alcohol with age checks, catering, business accounts, and couriers for other sellers.

features.name: Grocery and convenience shops
features.does: A shop lists thousands of items, and a picker and courier fill the order.

parts.name: Large catalogues
parts.what: Thousands of items with barcodes, categories and weights.

parts.name: Picker app
parts.what: A picking list with barcode scanning and swaps by the customer's own rules.

parts.name: Items sold by weight
parts.what: Price adjusted after picking, within a limit the customer agreed.

parts.name: Catalogue import
parts.what: Load a shop's product list from a spreadsheet or its stock system.

parts.name: Product recalls
parts.what: Items on the food regulator's recall list (example: New Zealand's MPI) are pulled from grocery listings, and buyers are told.

parts.name: Grocery information law
parts.what: The consumer information standards that cover groceries sold online, such as country of origin for some foods and unit pricing, and weights and measures law for items sold by weight.

features.name: Alcohol delivery
features.does: A customer of legal age orders alcohol from a licensed seller within the remote-sale rules, with ID checked at the door.

parts.name: Alcohol law study
parts.what: Remote sales under each country's alcohol law, starting with New Zealand's Sale and Supply of Alcohol Act 2012 and its regulations: what the seller and the platform must each do, and on which days and hours delivery is barred.

parts.name: Seller licence record
parts.what: Each seller's off-licence, its conditions and expiry.

parts.name: Age check at order
parts.what: Two age declarations made by the buyer in person, never by an AI agent, one on entering the store and one just before the sale, as the remote-sale regulations ask.

parts.name: ID check at the door
parts.what: The courier checks the receiver's ID, and that they are not intoxicated, before hand-over and records it; no ID means no hand-over.

parts.name: Refused delivery return
parts.what: Return refused alcohol to the seller, with the refund rules applied.

parts.name: Alcohol delivery hours
parts.what: Each country pack sets its own hours. In the first pack (New Zealand): no alcohol delivered from 11pm to 6am (section 59), none on Good Friday, Easter Sunday or Christmas Day or before 1pm on Anzac Day (section 48, which section 49 applies to remote-sale deliveries), and any narrower hours in the seller's licence conditions or a local alcohol policy that the law study finds apply.

parts.name: Licence on the page and receipt
parts.what: The licence holder's name, licence number and expiry on the store page and on every receipt, with an image of the licence or a link to one.

features.name: Catering and large orders
features.does: A business orders food for a group days ahead and gets an invoice.

parts.name: Large order rules
parts.what: Lead times, minimums and vehicle needs for big orders.

features.name: Business accounts
features.does: A company pays for staff meals with budgets and a monthly invoice.

parts.name: Food business accounts
parts.what: Food's meal budgets, allowed times and staff invites on the kit's business accounts on credit.

parts.name: Monthly invoicing
parts.what: Food's order lines on the kit's one monthly invoice with sales tax, paid by bank transfer.

features.name: Couriers for other sellers
features.does: A shop or restaurant with its own website books a Spare Food courier for its own orders.

parts.name: Delivery booking commands
parts.what: Book, track and pay for a Food courier through the command API, as Food's rules on a shared A-to-B delivery job type the kit must open, since Spare Market's shipping needs it too.

features.name: Parcels and errands
features.does: A person sends a small parcel across town with a courier.

parts.name: Parcel rules
parts.what: Food's size limits, banned items and proof of delivery for parcels, on the same shared A-to-B delivery job type the kit must open.

features.name: Medicines and other restricted goods
